This document is the fixture `tests/Quarto` renders. It is not documentation.
Each section exists because a test reads the rendered output and asserts on it,
so a cell removed from here fails a test rather than quietly reducing coverage.

The notebook sits one directory below the project that holds `composer.json` and
`vendor/`, so rendering it exercises the engine's walk up from the notebook's
own directory in search of an autoloader.

## Setup

The imports and the data load in a cell with `echo: false`, which keeps the
source out of the rendered page. A test asserts that none of this source
appears in the output.

```{php}
#| echo: false
use Phibble\DataFrame;
use Phiz\Datasets;
use Phiz\Plot;
use function Phplyr\{group_by, summarise, arrange, desc, n, mean};

$mpg = DataFrame::fromRows(Datasets::mpg());
```

## A phibble frame

A frame published as `text/html` becomes a table in the rendered page, with the
row and column counts and the per-column type abbreviations phibble's own
printing carries.

```{php}
$mpg
```

## A phplyr summary

The pipeline runs on the frame bound by the setup cell, which is how state
carries from one cell to the next.

```{php}
$by_class = $mpg
    |> group_by('class')
    |> summarise(count: n(), hwy: mean('hwy'))
    |> arrange(desc('hwy'));

$by_class
```

## A phiz plot

The plot publishes four representations. Quarto takes `text/html` for HTML
output and `image/svg+xml` for PDF, so the same cell is an interactive chart in
one format and a static figure in the other.

```{php}
#| fig-cap: "Highway mileage against engine displacement, by vehicle class."
Plot::of(Datasets::mpg())
    ->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy', color: 'class')
    ->point(opacity: 0.7)
    ->labs(x: 'Displacement (L)', y: 'Highway mpg');
```

## Several outputs from one cell

`Juphyter\display()` publishes a bundle part way through a cell, so one cell can
show more than one value.

```{php}
Juphyter\display($by_class |> arrange('hwy'));
Juphyter\display(['classes' => $by_class->nrow(), 'rows' => $mpg->nrow()]);
```

## State and a multibyte string

The variables bound above are still in scope, and a string outside ASCII
survives the round trip through the socket, the Jupyter message, and the
rendered page.

```{php}
$note = "Æthelred's résumé — 日本語";

echo mb_strlen($note), " characters, ", strlen($note), " bytes\n";

$note;
```

## A cell that raises

`error: true` lets the render continue past a failing cell and keeps the
traceback in the output. Both frames name the cell they came from rather than
`eval()'d code`, which is the rewriting the engine does to a traceback.

```{php}
#| error: true
$average = fn (array $values) => array_sum($values) / count($values);

$average([]);
```
